title: Supreme Court junks bid to question Duterte's arrest, ICC transfer
summary: The Supreme Court has dismissed the consolidated petitions for habeas corpus challenging the arrest and transfer of former President Rodrigo Duterte to the International Criminal Court.

blocks.text: Former President Rodrigo Duterte boards a chartered plane that is destined for The Hague, Netherlands.
Contributed photo via News5; former NICA director Alex Paul Monteagudo via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court has dismissed the consolidated petitions for habeas corpus challenging the arrest and transfer of former President Rodrigo Duterte to the International Criminal Court.
According to the Supreme Court, Philippine courts can no longer enforce the writ since Duterte is already detained in The Hague, the Netherlands.
Voting 9-4, the high court's en banc denied the petitions filed by Duterte's children — Sebastian, Veronica and Paolo — on their father's behalf.
The high court held that a writ of habeas corpus is strictly a domestic remedy that cannot be enforced beyond Philippine territory or against an international tribunal.

"Significantly, [Duterte] is not just beyond the Court's coercive powers, but also stands accused before an international tribunal that has assumed jurisdiction over his person," the Supreme Court said.
The high court also pointed out that Duterte is already actively participating in ICC proceedings and pursuing legal remedies there, rendering a domestic writ futile.

Furthermore, because the transfer had already been completed, the Philippine officials named in the petitions no longer hold custody or control over him and cannot be ordered to produce or release him.
The Supreme Court clarified that dismissing the petitions on mootness does not validate the legality of Duterte's arrest and surrender, nor does it mean his constitutional rights were not violated.
Rather, the ruling strictly addresses whether habeas corpus remains a viable remedy.
